messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard deviation (standard error) of the sampling distribution of the sample mean**

For a one‑sample test the standard error of the mean (SEM) is calculated as:

\[
\text{SEM} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
\(s\) = sample standard deviation = **1.4**  
\(n\) = sample size = **40**

\[
\text{SEM} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} = \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test (i.e., the standard error of the mean) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null hypothesis. That is indeed the standard error: sigma / sqrt(n). But they gave sample standard deviation 1.4. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. So answer ~0.2215.

Alternatively, if they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For a t-test, the standard deviation of the t-statistic under null is sqrt((n-1)/(n-2))? Actually t distribution has variance n-1/(n-3) for n>3. But likely they want standard error.

Thus answer: about 0.2215.

We can also compute p-value? But question only asks standard deviation. So answer: 0.2215.
